findings.where: the handwritten lines, at 300 per cent — 'it without' on the first line of the 'you made it without me' note, letters at x=534, x=641 and x=771, y=404-444; also crops/02_chat_300_hand.png
findings.what: Repeated letters are the same outline, not a variant of it: all seven isolated 't' components on this screen match one prototype at IoU 0.798-1.000 with a median outline-to-outline distance of 0.00 px and a mean of 0.14-0.35 px after best sub-pixel alignment, and three of them sit on one line 107 and 130 px apart; the same holds for the d/d, h/h, n/n and o/o pairs I checked (IoU 0.940-0.946, median outline distance 0.00 px), and 53 of the 148 handwritten letter components on the screen (35.8 per cent, delivery ticks excluded) fall into 22 groups that are pixel-identical at IoU >= 0.90.
findings.why: The row requires 'handwriting with multiple variants per glyph', judged at three hundred per cent on the Chat hero; at that zoom the hero shows exactly one form of 't' repeated six times across four notes, so the repeated letters are identical rather than varied.

findings.where: the exposed desk between y=400 and y=2600, which is about 55 per cent of that frame; same measurement on 02_chat.png and 01_pulse.png
findings.what: The desk grain has essentially no structure across the grain: over 110 tiles of 128 px that are entirely desk, the high-frequency power running across the strokes is 0.2 per cent of the power running along them (median ratio 0.002, p90 0.018; 0.003 in 02_chat and 01_pulse), i.e. no pores, no rays, no dust and no scratches crossing the grain — while blank paper in the same frames measures 0.53-0.60 on the equivalent minor/major axis ratio, i.e. a nearly isotropic felted tooth.
findings.why: The row's subject is whether a surface reads as photographed rather than simulated; the largest surface in every frame is a stroke-drawn wood, two orders of magnitude more one-directional than the paper lying on it, and the paper's photographic reading is asked to carry a substrate that measurably is not.

findings.where: MANIFEST.json 'stale' block; the file itself, and the three 300 per cent crops derived from it
findings.what: The still the row is judged on predates the capture: MANIFEST.json records 02_chat.png written 2026-09-08T18:50:07Z against a capture that began at 22:01:33Z, and lists thirteen of the fifteen present artifacts the same way (only 07_feeling_landing.mp4 is from this run). crops/02_chat_300_*.png were written at 22:18 but I verified them to be exact 3x nearest-neighbour crops of that older still at the boxes crops.json declares (mean absolute difference 0.00 across all three).
findings.why: Everything I measured about paper, tear, shadow and hand on the Chat hero describes a build at least three hours and eleven minutes older than the capture, so the row is scored on material that this run did not re-shoot.

findings.where: the bottom edges of the two wide strips centred at (702,1833) and (700,2216)
findings.what: One torn silhouette is used twice on a single screen: after removing each edge's own 61 px trend the two profiles agree to a mean absolute difference of 0.28 px over 1269 columns at a lag of 1 px (NCC 0.978) on a roughness of only 2.1 px rms — two independent edges of that roughness would differ by about 2.3 px. 13_messenger_states.png has a comparable pair at (751,446) and (747,1837), NCC 0.926.
findings.why: The row asks for 'tear masks with no visible repeat on a single screen'; this is that repeat, though the amplitude is 2 px so it is at the edge of what a reader would catch, and it is not on the Chat hero, where the eight sheets carry eight distinct silhouettes.

findings.where: the 'my brother has brought a dog' note around (700,1950) and the 'you narrated a soup' note around (1017,1036)
findings.what: One paper scan is repeated on the screen closely enough to align: logs/02_chat.report.json assigns stock lined_01 to three of the eight sheets and legal_01 to two more, and a dense normalised cross-correlation (self-match verified at 1.000) finds a 96x96 window of one note matching the other at 0.929, with 17 per cent of windows over that single alignment above 0.8 in a region of roughly 130x100 px.
findings.why: It is a repeat of one stock's grain and ruling within one frame; the amplitude is only about 1.5 grey levels rms on blank paper so it is below what a reader sees, but the row's standard is no repeat rather than no visible repeat once you are at three hundred per cent.

findings.where: absent, with 16_setup_android.png; reasons in MANIFEST.json and WHY_MISSING.json
findings.what: There is no picture of any of this material on Android. The reason given is measured rather than asserted — no /dev/kvm, the x86_64 image under QEMU instruction emulation, adbd answering after 113 minutes with no framework behind it — so nothing was faked from the PWA.
findings.why: Half the stated delivery target has no material evidence at all, so nothing in this row's judgement extends to the Android build; the reason is a reason, not an excuse, but the gap is still a gap.

what_is_working: No repeated noise field and no tiled texture anywhere I could find. Across 122 fully blank 64 px paper patches on the Chat hero, the best off-site grain match for any query patch is NCC 0.10-0.35; on nine stills the desk's strongest horizontal autocorrelation peak is 0.33 and the strongest vertical peak 0.33 (a tile would sit near 1.0), the best mirror-fold correlation is 0.81 in one 480 px window against 0.37-0.45 elsewhere, and the best translation repeat is 0.42. The below-floor clause is not triggered on any measurement I took.

No beige rounded rectangle stands in for paper in any of the ten stills. Blank paper carries 1.5 grey levels rms of tooth with a 2-3 px correlation length and a nearly isotropic spectrum (minor/major axis power ratio 0.53-0.60), and the printed rules are not drawn: on one sheet they deviate from a straight line by 0.3-2.0 px rms and their slopes differ from each other by up to 1.1 degrees, which is a warped photographed sheet rather than a repeating gradient.

Eight sheets on the Chat hero carry eight distinct tears. Comparing sub-pixel top-edge profiles pairwise over at least 400 px of overlap and all lags to plus or minus 450, the highest match is 0.806 and it collapses to -0.004 when the largest decile of excursions is removed, i.e. it is one shared feature, not a shared mask; every other pair is at or below 0.61. logs/02_chat.report.json independently names eight different masks from a pool of 56, and logs/tears.json agrees.

One light direction, and it holds. Nine sheets on the Chat hero cast their shadow at azimuths of 356-20 degrees (mean 9, from a column-normalised darkening field); 13_messenger_states.png gives eight sheets at mean 19.7 with a circular concentration of 0.943. The sheets' own rims agree with it: left rims run 4-16 grey levels below the sheet interior and right rims 8-14 above, which is what edges curling up under a key from the upper left do.

The contact shadows are not one blur. The falloff below the bottom edge peaks at about 4 px out on one note, 6-8 on another and 12-14 on a third, and depth varies along a single edge by an interquartile range of 30 grey levels. In 07_feeling_landing.mp4 the landing object's shadow rides in from far to the right and tightens against the object as it descends, which is a shadow that knows the object's height.

The unfolding clip is rendered geometry. Stepping frame by frame through the 139-frame run (16 ms a frame, playback_over_app_time 1.0), the opening panel's leading edge is tilted 70-102 px across the sheet's width while it is up and settles to 0.4-5 px when it lies down; the panel's mean luminance climbs 152 to 198 over the same frames, the sheet's projected height changes by 19 px, and the cast shadow beside it grows from 44,530 to 50,183 px while lightening from 80.4 to 84.6 grey levels. The panels carry paper tooth throughout, not a flat fill.

Feelings are objects. The Pulse row is six rendered things — a bent-wire chair on a torn scrap, a scribbled scrap, scattered confetti chips, a truncated cone with a pin, a wrapped sweet, a folded paper — each with its own shading and its own cast shadow, and crops/dusk_pulse.png re-lights the identical row coherently from the other side (shadows fall left and up in every object instead of right and down). No icon, no glyph, no sticker.

The evidence about itself checks out where I tested it. The three 300 per cent crops are exact 3x nearest-neighbour crops of 02_chat.png at the boxes logs/crops.json declares (mean absolute difference 0.00). My own independent hairline scan found no row brighter than both its neighbours over any 200 px run in any still — only darker rows, which are the printed rules — corroborating logs/hairline.json's zero.
verdict: The paper survives the test the row sets. I could not find the three things that would put this category under its floor: no repeated noise field (best off-site grain match on 122 blank patches, NCC 0.35), no tiled or mirrored desk (best autocorrelation peak 0.33 across nine stills), and no beige rectangle anywhere — blank stock carries 1.5 grey levels of nearly isotropic tooth and rules that wobble 0.3-2.0 px and disagree in slope by a degree across one sheet, which is a photographed warped page. The eight tears on the hero are eight tears; the one pair that correlated at 0.81 fell to zero when a single shared feature was removed. Nine sheets throw their shadows within a 24-degree arc and their rims shade to match, the penumbra differs in width from note to note rather than being one blur, and in 07 the landing object's shadow tightens as it comes down. In slow motion the unfold is geometry: a panel whose leading edge is tilted 100 px in perspective, brightening 152 to 198 as it turns into the light, with a cast shadow that grows and softens as it lays down. Two things hold it at the floor rather than above it. The first is the hand: at the three hundred per cent the row specifies, every isolated 't' on the Chat hero is one outline — median outline-to-outline distance 0.00 px — and three of them sit on one line of one note, so the letters repeat exactly where the row says to look for exactly that. The second is the desk: measured across the grain it has 0.2 per cent of the energy it has along it, no pores and nothing crossing the strokes, against 53-60 per cent isotropy for the paper lying on it, so the largest surface in every frame is drawn while the paper on it is scanned. Add that the hero I judged was written three hours and eleven minutes before the capture began, and that there is no Android frame at all, and this is a category that has earned its floor and not yet cleared it.
